name: Subiculum
synonyms: transitional cortex of the hippocampal formation
contextNote: A microscopic laminated hippocampal-field concept represented by an authored marker. The shape/coordinate does not establish CA/dentate/subicular boundaries; a host hippocampal mesh cannot independently validate a subfield segmentation. Named level membership is teaching/navigation metadata and has not been validated as a literal intersection of every displayed transverse section. The clinical text describes possible associations, not diagnostic rules.
function: The subiculum is transitional cortex between CA1 and the parahippocampal/entorhinal region. It receives hippocampal input and is a major source of output to entorhinal cortex, fornix and other cortical/subcortical memory networks. It is a laminated cortical field rather than a discrete spherical nucleus.

afferent: Other medial temporal and septal modulatory inputs
efferent: Fornix projections to mammillary, septal and anterior thalamic targets; other limbic outputs

bloodSupply: Shares mainly PCA hippocampal/temporal supply with variable anterior choroidal contribution.

clinical.findings: Can disrupt hippocampal output and memory, but an isolated subicular clinical syndrome cannot be inferred from a schematic marker.
Subicular/hippocampal circuits may participate in epileptic activity; onset must be established clinically and electrophysiologically.

refs: Blumenfeld, 2nd ed., pp. 830-838 and 842 (PDF pp. 856-864 and 868), Figures 18.8-18.13
Haines, Neuroanatomy: An Atlas of Structures, Sections, and Systems, 8th ed. (2012), pp. 74-79 (PDF pp. 88-93), Figures 5-1 to 5-6, coronal forebrain sections
Blumenfeld, 2nd ed., pp. 395-402 (PDF pp. 421-428), Figures 10.4-10.9; territories and collaterals vary

name: CA1 (Sommer sector)
contextNote: A microscopic laminated hippocampal-field concept represented by an authored marker. The shape/coordinate does not establish CA/dentate/subicular boundaries; a host hippocampal mesh cannot independently validate a subfield segmentation. Named level membership is teaching/navigation metadata and has not been validated as a literal intersection of every displayed transverse section. The clinical text describes possible associations, not diagnostic rules.
function: CA1 is a pyramidal-cell field between CA2 and subiculum. It receives CA3 Schaffer-collateral input and direct entorhinal input and relays to subiculum/entorhinal output networks. Its neurons are particularly vulnerable in some global ischemic and hippocampal-sclerosis patterns, for reasons not reducible to a fixed arterial watershed.
bloodSupply: Hippocampal PCA branches with variable anterior choroidal contribution; selective cellular vulnerability is not proof of a macroscopic border-zone location.

clinical.findings: CA1 injury can contribute to new-memory impairment; global injury may also affect other hippocampal fields, cortex and cerebellum.
CA1 cell loss/gliosis is prominent in common patterns, but sclerosis subtypes differ and MRI does not resolve every histological boundary.

name: CA2 and CA3 fields
contextNote: A microscopic laminated hippocampal-field concept represented by an authored marker. The shape/coordinate does not establish CA/dentate/subicular boundaries; a host hippocampal mesh cannot independently validate a subfield segmentation. Named level membership is teaching/navigation metadata and has not been validated as a literal intersection of every displayed transverse section. The clinical text describes possible associations, not diagnostic rules.
function: This atlas groups two distinct cytoarchitectural fields for display convenience. CA3 receives dentate mossy fibres and has recurrent excitatory circuitry; CA2 lies between CA3 and CA1 with distinct inputs and physiology. Experimental CA2 social-memory findings largely come from animal work and do not define a validated human lesion syndrome.

afferent: CA3: dentate mossy fibres, entorhinal and recurrent CA3 projections
CA2: entorhinal and other hippocampal/hypothalamic inputs; not equivalent to the CA3 mossy-fibre relay
efferent: CA3 Schaffer-collateral projections to CA1 and other hippocampal outputs
CA2 projections to CA1 and other hippocampal targets

bloodSupply: Shared hippocampal arterial territory, mainly PCA with variable anterior contribution.

clinical.findings: CA2/CA3 involvement varies; relative CA2 sparing is common in some patterns but is not guaranteed.
Selective CA2 manipulations affect social recognition in mice; direct extension to human psychiatric diagnoses remains uncertain.

name: CA4 (hilar field)
contextNote: A microscopic laminated hippocampal-field concept represented by an authored marker. The shape/coordinate does not establish CA/dentate/subicular boundaries; a host hippocampal mesh cannot independently validate a subfield segmentation. Named level membership is teaching/navigation metadata and has not been validated as a literal intersection of every displayed transverse section. The clinical text describes possible associations, not diagnostic rules.
function: CA4 is a historical cytoarchitectural label used for cells within the dentate hilus; the hilus also contains mossy cells and inhibitory interneurons, so the terms are not exact synonyms in every nomenclature. Local dentate/hilar circuits regulate excitation and sparse coding. This is a microscopic field, not a validated separate volume in the current atlas.

afferent: Dentate granule-cell mossy-fibre collaterals and local hippocampal inputs
efferent: Local hilar/dentate/CA3 circuits, depending on cell type

bloodSupply: Shared hippocampal arterial supply, mainly PCA branches with variable anterior contribution.

clinical.findings: Hilar/CA4 cell loss occurs in recognized sclerosis patterns, including CA4-predominant type; severity and clinical consequences vary.
Prolonged seizure activity may injure hippocampal cells, but hilar injury/sprouting is not a sufficient explanation for every subsequent epilepsy syndrome.
